name: Barbell Curl
description: The barbell curl is the foundational barbell biceps exercise, performed by curling a straight barbell from the thighs to the shoulders in a supinated grip. It allows maximal loading of the biceps brachii and brachialis and is one of the most effective exercises for overall biceps mass and strength development.

execution.starting_position: Stand with feet shoulder-width apart holding a barbell at hip height with a supinated grip slightly wider than shoulder width. Elbows tucked against the sides of the torso.
execution.setup_instructions: Use a straight barbell or EZ-curl bar. Keep the elbows pinned to the sides throughout the movement to isolate the biceps.
steps: Curl the barbell upward by flexing the elbows, keeping upper arms stationary.
Continue until the barbell is at shoulder height and the biceps are fully contracted.
Lower the barbell under control back to the starting position with full elbow extension.
execution.breathing_instructions: Exhale on the curl, inhale on the descent.
common_mistakes: Swinging the torso to generate momentum — keep the back straight
Allowing the elbows to drift forward, reducing biceps tension
Stopping short of full extension at the bottom
safety_considerations: If wrist discomfort occurs, switch to an EZ-curl bar
execution.range_of_motion_guidance: Full extension at the bottom, full flexion with biceps contracted at top.
coaching_cues: Keep your elbows glued to your sides — only your forearms should move
Squeeze hard at the top of each rep
